class.name: Netw
class.brief_description: Static entry points for the Networked API.
class.description: The interface provided by this class is optional and is supposed to work [u]with[/u] the default [SceneMultiplayer].

method.name: action
change_scene_to_file
method.description: Opens [param path] and makes players watch it. No node moves, spawn nodes from [signal NetwSessionHandle.scene_changed]. [param scope] says who watches and what retires. A server call always succeeds. A client call is a request that [method configure_scene_requests] decides, so a session declaring no [method configure_scene_requests] rejects it. [codeblock] var err: Error = await Netw.change_scene_to_file( self, "res://match.tscn").wait() if err != OK: status.text = "Could not start the match." [/codeblock]

method.name: change_scene_to_packed
method.description: The same change as [method change_scene_to_file], from a [PackedScene] that came from a file. A [PackedScene] built in memory is rejected.

method.name: channel
method.description: A [NetwChannel] for sending raw bytes in batches. [param channel_id] runs from [code]100[/code] to [code]254[/code]. [codeblock] var voice := Netw.channel(self, 100) voice.broadcast(frame, false) [/codeblock]

method.name: claim_authority
method.description: Asks the server to make this peer the [member NetwEntity.controller] of the entity [param node] belongs to, which is [method NetwEntity.claim_authority] reached from any node of it. [codeblock] Netw.claim_authority(self, NetwEntity.HOLD_YIELDABLE).then(pick_up) [/codeblock] A [param node] under no entity answers a promise rejected with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST]. [param hold] defaults to [constant NetwEntity.HOLD_EXCLUSIVE]. [b]Player request.[/b]

method.name: clock
method.description:
Returns the clock for the [member Node.multiplayer] of [param node]. [codeblock] @onready var clock := Netw.clock(self)
func _ready() -> void: clock.before_tick.connect(_sample_input) clock.on_tick.connect(_simulate) [/codeblock] [method configure_clock] is where the clock is set up before [member MultiplayerAPI.multiplayer_peer] connects.

method.name: configure_admission
method.description:
Gates if a [NetwPlayer] is created, arguments come from [method prepare_join]. Return [constant @GlobalScope.OK] to admit. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_admission(admit)
# Here `Netw.prepare_join` was called with `username` as the second argument with no extra arguments. func admit(peer_id: int, username: StringName) -> Error: if nakama.username_for_peer(peer_id) != username: return ERR_UNAUTHORIZED return OK [/codeblock] Use [member NetwMultiplayer.auth_callback] instead, as you would normally do with [SceneMultiplayer] to gate peers from entering the [MultiplayerAPI] such as to gate the firing of [signal MultiplayerAPI.peer_connected]. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: configure_clock
method.description: Sets up the clock for the [Node.multiplayer] and returns the [NetwClockConfig] to fill in. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_clock(self) \ .tickrate(60) \ .display_offset(2) [/codeblock] [param preset] can be used to [annotation GDScript.export] a [NetwClockConfig] from the inspector and declare it from [method Node._enter_tree] instead of [method Object._init].

method.name: configure_database
method.description:
Declares a [NetwDatabase] named [param name] on [member Node.multiplayer] of [param node]. [codeblock] func _ready() -> void: Netw.configure_database(self, &"saves").backend(preload("res://save_backend.tres")) [/codeblock] [method database] reaches the declared database. [param preset] copies an [annotation GDScript.export] [NetwDatabaseConfig]. If using [param preset], the recommended place to declare it is from [method Node._enter_tree]. [codeblock] @export var database_config: NetwDatabaseConfig
func _enter_tree() -> void: Netw.configure_database(self, &"saves", database_config) [/codeblock]

method.name: configure_despawn
method.description: Declares what the other peers do with [param node] when [method despawn] removes it. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_despawn(self).linger(0.5) [/codeblock]

method.name: configure_entity
method.description: Returns the [NetwEntity] that represents [param node] in the [member Node.multiplayer] session. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: var entity := Netw.configure_entity(self) # the node now behaves like `Node.set_multiplayer_authority(peer_id)` entity.initial_controller = NetwEntity.INITIAL_REPRESENTED_PEER [/codeblock]

method.name: configure_interest
method.description: Declares which [NetwInterestLayer] layer [param node] belongs to, and returns the [NetwInterestHandle] that is also [member NetwEntity.interest] of that [param node]. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_interest(self) \ .join( \ &"team:red", \ NetwMultiplayer.LEAVE_POLICY_RETAIN, \ NetwMultiplayer.PERCEPTION_POLICY_HIDE, \ ) \ .join(&"sight") \ .on_enter(_on_interest_enter) [/codeblock]

method.name: configure_join
method.description:
Declares what the server does with each peer that joins. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_join(spawn_at)
func spawn_at(who: NetwPlayer, point: StringName, team: int) -> void: arena.add_child(Netw.spawn_player(who, _spawn_avatar, team)) [/codeblock] [param handler] takes the [NetwPlayer] first, the rest of parameters are the areguments passed to [method prepare_join] before the [MultiplayerAPI] connected. [b]Note:[/b] the username passed to [method prepare_join] crosses as [member NetwPlayer.username]. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: configure_lagcomp
method.description: Tunes how far back the [NetwMultiplayer] records what every node held. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_lagcomp(self).input_gate_deadline(16) [/codeblock] Similarly to [method configure_clock], [param preset] can be used to [annotation GDScript.export] a [NetwLagCompensationConfig] from the inspector and declare it from [method Node._enter_tree] instead of [method Object._init].

method.name: configure_multiplayer_scene
method.description: Makes [param node] adopt a [NetwInterestLayer], children are automatically isolated from other multiplayer scenes. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_multiplayer_scene(self).labeled(&"Arena") [/codeblock]

method.name: configure_persistence
method.description: Declares which row of which [NetwDatabase] [param node] loads and saves from. [codeblock] func _ready() -> void: Netw.configure_property(self, &"gold") \ .persisted(game.save_schema.column_ref(0)) Netw.configure_persistence(self) \ .database(&"saves") \ .schema(game.save_schema) \ .record_id(account_name) [/codeblock] The declaration belongs to [param node] itself, so two entities running one script keep two record ids. Read [NetwPersistenceConfig] for what an entity declares, [NetwPersistenceHandle] for reaching the row, and [NetwDatabase] for the database architecture.

method.name: configure_property
method.description:
Declares how [param property] is synchronized. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_property(self, &"fuel")
func refuel() -> void: fuel = 100.0 Netw.sync_property(self, &"fuel") [/codeblock] [NetwPropertyConfig] documents every configuration and talks more about the replication model.

method.name: configure_rpc
configure_scene_requests
method.description:
Allows clients to request a scene change, and returns [constant @GlobalScope.OK] if the declaration was accepted. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_scene_requests(authorize_scene_request)
func authorize_scene_request( player: NetwPlayer, destination: String, scope: Netw.SceneChange ) -> Error: if scope != Netw.SCENE_CHANGE_PLAYER: return ERR_UNAUTHORIZED return OK if unlocked(player, destination) else ERR_UNAUTHORIZED [/codeblock] [param handler] is called on the server for every client request.

method.name: configure_schema
method.description:
Declares a schema for a table of records. [codeblock] class Mobs: static var schema := Netw.configure_schema(&"Mob") static var pos := schema.vector3(&"pos") static var hp := schema.u16(&"hp")
@onready var mobs := Netw.table(self, &"Mob") [/codeblock] Schemas are used for creating [NetwTableHandle] instances.

method.name: configure_server_info
method.description:
Declares what this server says about itself when another peer probes it with [method NetwConnectHandle.endpoint_probe]. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_server_info(server_info)
func server_info(info: NetwServerInfo) -> NetwServerInfo: info.motd = "Friday night session" info.max_players = 8 return info [/codeblock]

method.name: configure_session
method.description: Configures the [Node.multiplayer] session with extra settings that [SceneMultiplayer] does not cover. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_session(self) \ .app_id(&"bomber-v2") \ .desired_role(NetwMultiplayer.ROLE_LISTEN_SERVER) [/codeblock] For more information on the available settings, see [NetwSessionConfig].

method.name: configure_signal
method.description: Registers [param sig] so [method emit_entity_signal] may emit it on every peer. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_signal(self.exploded) # only the server may emit it [/codeblock] A signal registered here defaults to [method NetwMemberConfig.call_local], so emitting it fires the local listeners as well. [method configure_rpc] and [method configure_property] default the other way, to [method NetwMemberConfig.call_remote].

method.name: configure_spawn
method.description:
Registers [param callable] as a function [method spawn] may run on every peer to build the same node. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_spawn(_spawn_bullet)
func _spawn_bullet(dir: Vector2, tier: int) -> Node: var bullet := BulletScene.instantiate() bullet.setup(dir, tier) return bullet
# ...
var bullet := Netw.spawn(_spawn_bullet, dir, tier) # server only muzzle.add_child(bullet)
# Clients -> build the same node with the same arguments and mount it in the same place [/codeblock]

method.name: connection
database
method.description: The [NetwDatabase] declared under [param name] in [param node]'s session. Returns the same cached handle on every call. [codeblock] var db: NetwDatabase = Netw.database(self, &"saves") [/codeblock] [method configure_database] declares [param name] first.

method.name: despawn
method.description: Removes the node [method spawn] or [method replicate] made, on every peer. [codeblock] Netw.despawn(bullet) [/codeblock] [param opts] configures what happens to the node on every peer, see [NetwDespawnOpts] for the options. It returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST] for a node that is not a spawned one and [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE] for a node in no [MultiplayerAPI]. The session authority may always call it, and the [member NetwEntity.controller] may for a node whose [member NetwEntity.lifecycle] is [constant NetwEntity.LIFECYCLE_CONTROLLER]. The node leaves the controller's peer at once, and the server serves it back if it refuses.

method.name: emit_entity_signal
method.description:
Emits [param sig] on every peer, including the local one, with the arguments that follow. [codeblock] signal exploded(position: Vector2)
func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_signal(self.exploded)
# ...
# `exploded` emits on every peer and also locally Netw.emit_entity_signal(self.exploded, position) [/codeblock] A registered signal fires locally as well, so calling [code]sig.emit()[/code] beside this would fire the local listeners twice.

method.name: prepare_join
method.description: Asks the session for a place in the game as [param username]. Every argument after the username reaches the [method configure_join] handler after its [NetwPlayer]. [codeblock] Netw.prepare_join(self, &"Dev", &"red") multiplayer.multiplayer_peer = peer [/codeblock] Call it before or after the [member MultiplayerAPI.multiplayer_peer] is assigned. The [NetwPromise] reports local preparation, [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE] for a failure to submit, and [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_ALREADY_IN_USE] for a duplicate request. An empty [param username] is rejected with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER]. [b]Player request.[/b]

method.name: of
method.description: The [NetwMultiplayer] running the [member Node.multiplayer] is in. [codeblock] var api := Netw.of(self) api.entity_despawn(route) [/codeblock] A node that is in no tree returns [code]null[/code].

method.name: release_authority
method.description: Hands control of the entity [param node] belongs to on to [param successor], or to the server when it is [code]0[/code], with this peer's final state. It is [method NetwEntity.release_authority] reached from any node of it. A [param node] under no entity answers a promise rejected with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST]. [b]Player request.[/b]

method.name: reload_current_scene
method.description: Opens the scene this peer presents again, the way [method SceneTree.reload_current_scene] does.

method.name: reparent
method.description: Moves [param node] under [param new_parent] the way [method Node.reparent] does, and answers a [NetwPromise] that resolves once the session authority holds the node under its new parent. Every other peer that holds the node takes the move after that. [codeblock] await Netw.reparent(body, level2.get_node(^"Players")).wait() [/codeblock] What it adds over [method Node.reparent] is a window that masks the mover off the physics server across the parent swap, basically a workaround for this [url=https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/14578]issue[/url]. [method Node.reparent] stays fully supported and is the right verb for anything that doesn't depend on area signals. A [param node] that is no entity answers [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST] and one in no session answers [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE]. The session authority may always call it, and the [member NetwEntity.controller] may for a node whose [member NetwEntity.lifecycle] is [constant NetwEntity.LIFECYCLE_CONTROLLER]. The controller's move lands on its own peer at once, and a refusal from the server rejects the promise and moves the node back. At most eight such moves of one entity wait on the server at a time, and the ninth is moved back and rejected with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE].

method.name: replicate
method.description: Sends a node the game built itself to every peer, which rebuild it from its [member Node.scene_file_path], and returns its [NetwEntity]. [param node] has no parent yet. [member NetwEntity.route], [member NetwEntity.entity_id], [member NetwEntity.peer_id] and [member NetwEntity.controller] are all filled in by the time this returns, and the other peers are not told anything until the node enters the tree. That gap is where the node's first values are written. [codeblock] var body := PlayerScene.instantiate() var entity := Netw.replicate(body, player) body.position = spawn_point scene.add_child(body) [/codeblock] The session authority may always call it, and a client may with no [param owner] when [param node] declares [member NetwEntity.lifecycle] as [constant NetwEntity.LIFECYCLE_CONTROLLER], becoming its [member NetwEntity.controller].

method.name: request
method.description: Calls [param callable] on the server and returns a [NetwPromise] carrying what it returned. [codeblock] var sold: bool = await Netw.request(shop.buy, &"shield").wait() [/codeblock] Register the method with [method configure_rpc] first, the same as [method rpc].

method.name: request_all
method.description: Calls [param callable] on every peer that can see the node, and returns a [NetwGroupPromise] gathering what they each returned. Which peers are waited for is decided when the call goes out, so a peer arriving afterwards is not one of them.

method.name: request_controller
method.description: Calls [param callable] on the peer driving the node, its [member NetwEntity.controller].

method.name: request_id
method.description: Calls [param callable] on [param peer_id] alone and returns a [NetwPromise] carrying what it returned. A [param peer_id] of [code]0[/code] is rejected, since asking everyone is [method request_all].

method.name: rewind
method.description: Puts every entity in [param entities] back where it was at [param tick], runs [param body] against that older world, then returns them all to where they are now. [codeblock] func _fire(ctx: NetwActionContext) -> void: Netw.rewind(Netw.scene(self).entities, ctx.view_tick, _trace_shot) [/codeblock]

method.name: rpc
method.description: Calls [param callable] on every peer that can see the node. [codeblock] Netw.rpc(turret.aim, yaw) [/codeblock]

method.name: rpc_controller
method.description: Calls [param callable] on the peer driving the node, its [member NetwEntity.controller].

method.name: rpc_id
method.description: Calls [param callable] on [param peer_id] alone, or on every connected peer when [param peer_id] is [code]0[/code].

method.name: sample
scene
method.description: The [NetwSceneHandle] for a multiplayer scene, a node with a [NetwInterestLayer] and a [NetwSceneConfig]. When [param named] is not given, the closest [NetwSceneHandle] ancestor is returned. [codeblock] var here := Netw.scene(self) # the scene I am in var arena := Netw.scene(spawned) # the one I just spawned var track := Netw.scene(self, &"Track") # the only live Track [/codeblock]

method.name: service
method.description: Services are objects tied to [member Node.multiplayer] lifecycle, similar to singletons but per [MultiplayerAPI]. [codeblock] var gamestate := Netw.service(self, MyGamestate) as MyGamestate [/codeblock] A session holding nothing under [param type] returns [code]null[/code].

method.name: service_register
method.description: Registers [param service] with the [member Node.multiplayer], so [method service] finds it. [codeblock] Netw.service_register(self, MyGamestate.new()) [/codeblock] [param type] defaults to the class of [param service], so a session may hold one instance of each class. A session holding a service under [param type] already replaces it with the new one.

method.name: service_unregister
method.description: Unregisters [param service] from the [member Node.multiplayer], so [method service] no longer finds it.

method.name: session
method.description: The [NetwSessionHandle] of the [member Node.multiplayer]. Mostly useful for connecting signals. [codeblock] var s := Netw.session(self) s.entered.connect(_on_entered) s.disconnected.connect(_on_over) s.ended.connect(_on_over) [/codeblock]

method.name: spawn
method.description: Builds the same node on every peer by running [param fn] with the arguments given after it, and returns this peer's copy for the caller to parent. [codeblock] muzzle.add_child(Netw.spawn(_spawn_bullet, dir, 2)) [/codeblock] Register [param fn] with [method configure_spawn] first, and parent the node returned before the next tick. The session authority may always call it, and a client may when the node [param fn] builds declares [member NetwEntity.lifecycle] as [constant NetwEntity.LIFECYCLE_CONTROLLER], becoming its [member NetwEntity.controller]. The node shows on that client at once, and is removed if the server refuses it.

method.name: spawn_player
method.description: Builds the node [param player] drives, the same way [method spawn] builds any other. [codeblock] players.add_child( Netw.spawn_player(player, _spawn_avatar, character_class) ) [/codeblock] The node becomes tied to [param player] lifecycle. A node that declares [method NetwPersistenceConfig.load_on_spawn] reaches the other peers once its stored row is applied. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: table
method.description:
The [NetwTableHandle] for the replicated table declared under [param name]. [codeblock] @onready var mobs := Netw.table(self, &"Mob")
func _ready() -> void: mobs.received.connect(_on_mobs) [/codeblock] [method configure_schema] is where [param name] is declared.

method.name: sync_property
method.description: Sends what [param property] is holding right now to the other peers, for a property that changes on events rather than every tick. [codeblock] func refuel() -> void: fuel = 100.0 Netw.sync_property(self, &"fuel") [/codeblock] [method configure_property] must be declared first.

constants.constant: All peers watch the destination multiplayer scene.
The local peer watches the destination multiplayer scene.
All peers from the same scene the requester node is in watch the destination multiplayer scene.
The multiplayer scene shares the physics and render world of whatever it is parented into.
The multiplayer scene simulates in a world of its own using a [SubViewport], so geometry overlapping another scene's cannot interact with it.
